newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU in more infringement cases against member states.
newsitem.headline: EU in more infringement cases against member states.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday the number of new legal proceedings against member states for not complying with EU law increased last year, even though the number of complaints dropped sharply.
The European Union executive said it started 846 infringement cases by sending so-called letters of formal notice to member states, an increase of nine percent from 1995.

In addition, it issued 53 reasoned opinions, which represent the second step in EU infringement proceedings. This was an increase of 224 percent compared with 1995, the Commission said in a statement.

"This was made possible by the steps taken by the Commission to improve the operation and effectiveness of the infringement procedure," it said. "They resulted in faster, simpler and clearer management of infringements."
Also in 1996, the number of complaints against member states not complying with EU legislation declined by 14 percent to 819.

"Examination of these figures by sector reveals a sharp fall in the number of complaints and the number of cases detected by the Commission relating to the environment and a small drop in the number relating to the single market," the Commission said.
It also said member states had improved their performance when it came to implementing EU directives.
"There is still cause for concern in some areas, in particular for certain old directives such as those concerning public procurement," it said.
